description: Cohesive frontend visual + design-system overhaul. Replace the current dull/dark muted-forest-green look with a vibrant, lively, professional multi-hue MOUNTAIN palette (alpine/Himalayan: crisp fresh/teal-leaning greens, a vivid sky/glacier blue, warm sunrise/golden-hour accents, a cool slate for depth), introduce a real typography pairing via next/font (expressive display font for headings + clean readable sans for body), and add life (stronger hierarchy, more generous spacing, refined cards/shadows, coloured accents/badges/charts/stat tiles, hover/transition polish). Keep the Uttarakhand/Mussoorie hill-town identity but make it vivid, not drab. Centralise everything in the three theme files + shared primitives so all 18 pages inherit the refresh. This is a design-system redesign, not a one-off tweak.
steps: PALETTE STRATEGY (keeps everything in sync and avoids mass breakage): KEEP the existing Tailwind color-scale token NAMES (forest, mist, pine, dawn) and the lib/theme.ts palette export KEYS (forest.DEFAULT/deep/mid/bright, mist.DEFAULT/white/haze, pine, dawn, ink) so the ~73 files that reference them and the chart imports keep working — but REPLACE THEIR VALUES with the new vibrant palette. The current forest is a muted dark green (700 approx #275233, deep #1c3725, bright #3f8150) — the user explicitly dislikes this 'dull green'. Shift 'forest' to a crisper, fresher, more alpine green (brighter, slightly cooler/teal-leaning, higher saturation) across the full 50-950 scale, keeping good contrast at 700/800 for text-on-light and light tints at 50-200 for backgrounds. Make 'pine' a livelier accent green and 'dawn' a warmer, more vivid sunrise/golden-hour amber. ADD at least two NEW multi-hue accent color scales to tailwind.config.ts (and mirror in globals.css CSS vars + lib/theme.ts palette) for the multi-hue system the brief asks for: e.g. a vivid 'sky'/'glacier' blue scale and a cool 'slate'/'stone' scale for depth. Use these new accents on cards/badges/charts/stat tiles so the UI is multi-hue, not one-green-everywhere. Do NOT remove or rename existing tokens; only add new ones and re-value existing ones.

Update ALL THREE theme files together and keep them mirrored: frontend/tailwind.config.ts (color scales, boxShadow ridge/tile, backgroundImage hill-haze + forest-header, and ADD a display font family e.g. fontFamily.display bound to a new --font-display var while keeping fontFamily.sans=var(--font-sans)); frontend/app/globals.css (CSS variables mirroring the new palette, the base layer, and the .ridge-divider motif — refresh gradients to be livelier); frontend/lib/theme.ts (palette object values + add new accent keys; keep brand/navItems structural exports stable). Refresh backgroundImage gradients (hill-haze body background, forest-header sidebar gradient) to be more vivid/alpine (e.g. a sky-to-green dawn gradient) while staying professional.

TYPOGRAPHY: wire next/font in frontend/app/layout.tsx. Import an expressive display/heading font and a clean readable body sans from next/font/google (choose a professional pairing with good Latin + ideally Devanagari coverage since the product shows Hindi/Devanagari text; if a single face lacks Devanagari, that is acceptable for this pass). Expose them as CSS variables: set body font to --font-sans and the display font to a --font-display variable, applying the variable classNames on <html> or <body>. Ensure tailwind.config.ts fontFamily.sans uses var(--font-sans) (already does) and fontFamily.display uses var(--font-display). Update globals.css headings (h1,h2,h3) and/or PageHeader to use the display font. Verify the build still succeeds offline/with network (next/font/google downloads at build time; OPEN_INTERNET is available).

Propagate the look through shared primitives so every page benefits at once: frontend/components/ui/{Badge,Button,Card,PageHeader,StatTile,Table}.tsx and index.ts — refine with the new palette, coloured accents, better radius/shadow, hover/transition polish, nicer empty/stat states; use the new accent hues (e.g. sky/slate) in addition to green so tiles/badges/charts are multi-hue. StatTile: keep it lively (coloured trend states) but ensure the Badge default tone keeps a class containing 'text-forest-800' (see guardrail) unless the test is updated accordingly.

frontend/components/layout/{AppShell,Header,Sidebar}.tsx — give the shell a more vivid, professional mountain feel: Sidebar still uses bg-forest-header (now a livelier gradient) and the brand block; add tasteful depth/accents; improve active/hover nav states; keep the brand block and navItems-driven structure.

frontend/components/charts/{LineChart,Sparkline}.tsx and frontend/components/common/{Drilldown,MiniTrend}.tsx — drive colours from the refreshed palette (import from lib/theme.ts); give charts a lively multi-hue series palette (greens + sky blue + sunrise amber + slate) instead of mostly-green, keeping the credible-interval band and grid readable.

GUARDRAIL — keep tests green by updating them intentionally, not deleting coverage: run `npx vitest run` after changes. The tests that assert on markup/classes are frontend/components/ui/StatTile.test.tsx (asserts a default Badge className contains 'text-forest-800'), frontend/components/market-radar/ReviewCountsTable.test.tsx (asserts rendered text like 'Pine View Inn', 'Google', '5', 'No reviews collected yet.', 'Parking', '23'), frontend/app/(dashboard)/deep-pages.test.tsx and frontend/app/(dashboard)/sentinel-destination-pages.test.tsx (assert rendered page content). If an intentional markup/class change breaks an assertion, UPDATE the assertion to match the new intended output rather than removing the test. Prefer keeping the 'forest' token name and the Badge default-tone 'text-forest-800' class so StatTile.test.tsx stays green without edits.

GUARDRAIL — token integrity: because token NAMES are preserved, no mass rename is needed. If you DO rename/remove any Tailwind color token, you MUST update all three theme files AND every usage across components/ and app/ (grep for the token name) so nothing references a dropped token. Confirm with a grep that no removed token name remains.

Run the full frontend gate: `npm run lint && npx vitest run && npm run build`. All must pass (build should still produce ~21 routes). Fix any Tailwind class references to tokens, any TypeScript errors from palette shape changes, and any lint issues.
acceptance_criteria: The three theme files (tailwind.config.ts, globals.css, lib/theme.ts) are mutually consistent: every CSS var / Tailwind token / palette key referenced by components exists in all the places that need it.

The palette is visibly a vibrant multi-hue mountain system (fresher green + at least two new accent hues such as sky/glacier blue and slate), not the old muted dark forest green; the dull forest.700~#275233 / deep ~#1c3725 values are replaced with brighter alpine values.

A real font pairing is wired via next/font in app/layout.tsx: --font-sans (body) and a --font-display (headings) are set and used; headings render in the display font. The app no longer silently falls back to system-ui because --font-sans was never set.

Shared primitives (Badge, Button, Card, PageHeader, StatTile, Table), the layout shell (AppShell, Header, Sidebar), charts (LineChart, Sparkline) and common (Drilldown, MiniTrend) all consume the refreshed tokens, so the refresh is visible across all 18 dashboard pages without per-page restyling.
lib/theme.ts keeps stable export shapes (palette keys used by charts + brand + navItems) — charts still import palette.forest.*, palette.mist.*, palette.ink, etc. without TypeScript errors.
`npm run lint` passes, `npx vitest run` passes (any tests broken by intentional markup/class changes are updated, not deleted), and `npm run build` succeeds building ~21 routes.
verification: grep that any removed/renamed token name no longer appears in app/ or components/ (only if tokens were renamed)
findings:
Delivered the vibrant multi-hue alpine design-system overhaul. All token NAMES and lib/theme.ts palette export KEYS were kept stable (forest.DEFAULT/deep/mid/bright, mist.DEFAULT/white/haze, pine, dawn, ink) and re-valued; two new accent scales (sky, slate) were ADDED to all three theme files + the palette object. No tokens were removed/renamed, so no mass rename was needed and no test markup edits were required (StatTile.test.tsx still passes because the default Badge tone keeps 'bg-forest-100 text-forest-800 border-forest-200').

NEW PALETTE (hex): forest 50 #e8faf1,100 #c6f3dd,200 #8ee7bd,300 #54d79a,400 #28c483,500 #17b47f,600/700 #1f8a5b,800 #166b4a,900 #0f5f44,950 #063b2b (crisp teal-leaning alpine green, replaces old muted #275233/#1c3725). mist 50 #fbfdfd,100 #f1f7f6,200 #e2efed,300 #cde3df,400 #aecfc9,white #fbfdfd. pine 400 #2fd79a,500 #17b47f,600 #108a63. dawn 400 #ffc14d,500 #f6a623,600 #e08a0b (vivid golden-hour amber). NEW sky (glacier blue) 50 #e8f6fd..400 #38bdf8,500 #1d9bd1,600 #0c6fa0,700 #0a567c. NEW slate 50 #f1f5f7..400 #7a94a3,500 #4b6472,600 #39505c,700 #2b3f4a,800 #1d2d35. lib/theme.ts palette mirrors: forest.DEFAULT #1f8a5b/deep #0f5f44/mid #179467/bright #28c483; mist.DEFAULT #f1f7f6/white #fbfdfd/haze #e2efed; pine #17b47f; dawn #f6a623; ink #123b2f; sky.DEFAULT #1d9bd1/deep #0c6fa0/bright #38bdf8; slate.DEFAULT #4b6472/deep #2b3f4a/bright #7a94a3. Gradients refreshed: hill-haze = glacier-to-meadow-to-sky; forest-header sidebar = sky-blue sweeping into deep green; new dawn-ridge sky->green->sunrise accent used on StatTile top bar; .ridge-divider is now a sky->green->sunrise sweep.

TYPOGRAPHY: wired next/font/google in app/layout.tsx — Inter as body (--font-sans) and Poppins (500/600/700) as the expressive display face (--font-display); both variable classes applied on <html>. tailwind.config fontFamily.sans=var(--font-sans) (kept) + new fontFamily.display=var(--font-display). globals.css sets body font-family to var(--font-sans) and h1/h2/h3 to var(--font-display); PageHeader/Card titles/Table headers/StatTile values/Sidebar brand/Header title use font-display. This closes the gap where --font-sans was never set and the app fell back to system-ui.

PRIMITIVES/CHARTS CHANGED: ui/{Badge (added sky+slate tones, kept forest default text-forest-800),Button (hover glow + sky secondary),Card (brighter mist-white surface, hover shadow-ridge, display titles),PageHeader (sky eyebrow, 3xl display title),StatTile (dawn-ridge accent bar, lift-on-hover, display value),Table (uppercase display headers, sky-50 row hover)}; layout/{Header (sky eyebrow + sky Demo badge + display title),Sidebar (display brand, dawn-ring active nav state), AppShell unchanged}; charts/{LineChart,Sparkline both already palette-driven — auto-updated}; common/{MiniTrend (palette.mist.haze axis), Drilldown unchanged - uses tokens}. Chart series colours in TrendsPanel, forecast/page, proof-of-impact/page updated from stale old hexes (#275233/#dca24c/#9cc3a5/#c0563b) to multi-hue palette.forest/dawn/sky/slate. Minor stale hexes in time-machine (text-dawn-600) and HotspotMap (#0f5f44 select ring, #e2efed bg) refreshed.

TESTS: no test files modified — all 14 remained green as-is (preserved forest token + text-forest-800 default, and all asserted rendered text unchanged).

FINAL GATES (all PASS): npm run lint = No ESLint warnings or errors; npx vitest run = 14 passed (4 files); npm run build = compiled + 21 routes generated (next/font/google downloaded fonts at build time under OPEN_INTERNET). Grep confirmed no dropped/stale token names or old-palette hexes remain in app/ or components/.
